### Observed differences

- The clearest difference lies in how the block A23–A30–A31–A24 is traversed. In the earlier window, after A23 about 52 in 100 continuations went directly to A31 and about 46 to A30; in the later window this reversed to about 42 and 55. After A30, the share continuing to A31 rose from about 47 to 56 in 100 while the exit to A24 fell from about 52 to 43; after A31, the exit to A24 rose from about 47 to 54 while the return to A30 fell from about 53 to 43. All four activities occur in essentially every trace in both windows, and each shift is larger than in about 90–95 of 100 random re-splits of the same data. [DIR023, DIR030, DIR031]
- A same-shaped shift appears around A20, A22 and A28: after A20, the share continuing to A22 rose from about 22 to 35 in 100 while the share going to A28 fell from about 57 to 43; after A22, the share going on to A28 rose from about 47 to 59 while the share returning to A20 fell from about 28 to 16. Both sources are observed in roughly half of all traces in both windows. [DIR020, DIR022]
- Successor shares also moved in other well-observed places: after A02 and after A10, continuations shifted away from A15 and A42 toward A16 and A23 (A02→A16 rose from about 8 to 24 in 100, A10→A42 fell from about 32 to 18); around A01, A05, A07, A09 and A14 the chain A01→A09→A05→A07→A14 gained against the reverse and shortcut edges (A05→A07 rose from about 23 to 37 in 100, A09→A14 fell from about 34 to 24); after A13 the share going to A12 fell from about 42 to 26 in 100 while shares to A11 and A14 rose, whereas after A03 the share to A12 rose from about 28 to 39. [DIR002, DIR010, DIR001, DIR005, DIR007, DIR009, DIR013, DIR003]
- Participation itself changed only slightly: A10 appeared in about 12 of 100 traces before and about 17 in 100 later, A40 rose from about 57 to 63 and A13 from about 49 to 54, while A07 fell from about 52 to 48 and A35 from 50 to 45; each of these differences is matched or exceeded in roughly a quarter to a third of random re-splits, so none is unusual on its own. [OCC010, OCC036, OCC013, OCC007, OCC031]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, existing alternative routes are taken with different frequencies, while every activity and edge involved remains in use — a shift between existing paths rather than a replacement of one path by another. Most clearly, the step sequence A23→A30→A31→A24 was completed more often, at the expense of entering the block directly at A31 (A23→A31), leaving it early (A30→A24) and looping back from A31 to A30; around A20, A22 and A28 the route via A22 (A20→A22→A28) likewise gained against the direct edge A20→A28 and the return edge A22→A20. The supporting signs are that all involved activities and edges are observed in both windows with substantial support (about 90–200 traces per window), the shifts within each block all point one way, and each is larger than in about 90 of 100 random re-splits, which makes pure sampling noise an unlikely explanation for the blocks as a whole. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a change in the mix of cases reaching these blocks from upstream, which would shift successor shares without any local routing change; the evidence also reports no screening baseline, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with the expectation for an unchanged process. [DIR023, DIR030, DIR031, DIR020, DIR022]

Other differences: after A02 and A10, successor shares moved from A15 and A42 toward A16 and A23; around A01, A05, A07, A09 and A14 the chain A01→A09→A05→A07→A14 gained against the reverse and shortcut edges; after A13 continuations shifted from A12 toward A11 and A14, while after A03 they shifted from A11 toward A12. [DIR002, DIR010, DIR001, DIR005, DIR007, DIR009, DIR013, DIR003]

Participation shifted only slightly and in both directions (A03, A10, A13 and A40 up by about 4–6 in 100 traces; A07, A18, A34 and A35 down by about 4–5), and the largest raw redirection, after A44, rests on only 8–9 observed outgoing transitions and is not unusual against random re-splits, so it carries no weight. [OCC003, OCC007, OCC010, OCC013, OCC018, OCC030, OCC031, OCC036, DIR044]
